newsitem.title: ITALY: AT&T could enter Stet capital - minister.
newsitem.headline: AT&T could enter Stet capital - minister.

text.p: Italian Posts and Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico said on Wednesday U.S. telecoms group AT&T could become a stable shareholder in Italian state telecoms holding Stet once it has been privatised.
Asked on the fringes of a meeting whether AT&T could enter a stable core of Stet shareholders with a five percent stake, Maccanico replied it was "certainly possible".
Stet is due to be privatised in the autumn. It plans to hold a "very important" news conference at 1500 GMT today.
Michele Lauria, undersecretary at the post and telecommunications ministry, told Reuters on Tuesday an announcement on a long-awaited deal with AT&T was imminent.
Approval for a company like AT&T to take a five percent stake in Stet would have to come from the telecom holding's majority shareholder, which is the Italian Treasury.
Stet's statutes envisage a maximum three percent stake for private shareholders with the possibility of five percent with Treasury approval.
Italian media have speculated that the two companies might initially seek co-operation deals around the world, including South America, where Stet has a particularly strong presence.
As part of a second phase, there would be a share swap, with AT&T set to become part of Stet's core shareholder structure following the Italian firm's selloff, slated for October.
Maccanico called the expected accord "important and very positive", adding that it would change the landscape of the telecoms sector in Italy.
If the expected deal goes ahead it is likely to provide Stet with the kind of international alliance it has been seeking for years to turn it into a major player on the world stage.

Stet, which is set to merge with fixed line operator Telecom Italia on July 18, has a limited deal with International Business Machines Corp and linked up earlier this year with AT&T to bid in the privatisation of Brazil's mobile phone market.
Under the terms of the deal expected to be unveiled on Wednesday, Stet is also expected to replace Spain's Telefonica in the AT&T-directed European telecoms consortium, Unisource.

Telefonica had a 25 percent stake in Unisource which groups Sweden's Telia, Swiss Telecom and Koninklijke PTT Nederland, but decided to quit the project and join forces with AT&T's rival MCI Communications Corp in the U.S.

In the event of a Stet/AT&T deal, analysts believe Unisource would join a consortium which includes the Italian conglomerate and numerous Spanish firms in bidding for Spain's second domestic telephone operator, Retevision RET.CN.
Unisource originally entered the race for Retevision, but was not among the three consortia shortlisted. A final decision on the sale is due shortly with the Stet bid seen well placed.
Unisource is seen as one of the world's three major telecoms alliances, alongside Global One and the British Telecom MCI Communications Concert alliance.

One of the major difficulties faced by negotiators trying to stitch up a deal between Stet and AT&T has been the conflict of interest between their various European operations, particularly in Germany.
AT&T has already established ties with Mannesmann, while Stet has always been keen on links with Veba.

Stet shares climbed nearly four percent on the Milan stock market earlier but had retraced to stand 2.54 percent up at 10250 lire by 1030 GMT. The bourse itself is more than one percent up on the day.
--Milan bureau +392 66129507
